rules.title: Security Deposit Trust and Investment Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlord must hold deposit in trust, not commingled with landlord's assets. For 10 or fewer units: insured bank/S&L in NJ, interest-bearing account. For 10+ units: option of insured money market fund (NJ company, 1-year maturity) or insured bank/S&L with variable rate interest. Seasonal rentals (≤125 consecutive days) exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must 
deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an 
interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit. A landlord or designee 
who receives security deposit money for 10 or more units has the option of investing the money in 
an insured money market fund of a New Jersey-based investment company where the investments 
mature in one year or less, or deposit that money in a State or federally charted bank, or savings, 
and loan association located in New Jersey in an account bearing a variable rate of intere st.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all deposits; different requirements based on number of units controlled by landlord; NJ location required
rules.sanctions: Penalties for misuse or commingling of deposits

rule.title: Unconscionable Rent Increase Standard
rule.requirement: Rent increases must not be unconscionable, defined as so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person. Factors include: amount of increase, landlord's expenses and profitability, comparison to similar properties, and relative bargaining position.
rule.citation: Fromet Properties v. Buel, 294 N.J. Super. 601 (App. Div. 1996); Hale v. Farrakhan, 390 N.J. Super. 335 (App. Div. 2007)

rule.title: Reprisal Protection - Retaliation Prohibited
rule.requirement: Landlord cannot take reprisal action (eviction, substantial lease alteration, or refusal to renew) against tenant exercising civil rights: (1) enforcing lease/law rights; (2) making good faith complaint to government about landlord violations (after notifying landlord in writing); (3) organizing/joining lawful tenant organizations; (4) refusing changes made in retaliation.

A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit if it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent when combined with the regular security deposit.

rule.title: Security Deposit Return - 30 Day Requirement
rule.requirement: Within 30 days after tenancy termination, landlord must return security deposit plus interest earned less deductions by personal delivery, registered, or certified mail. Itemized deduction list must accompany deductions by registered/certified mail within 30 days of termination. No deductions from deposits of tenants who remain in possession.
rule.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1). Deductions may include the cost of any damages over and above normal wear and tear, and any other money due the landlord under the terms of the lease. The landlord must return the money either by personal delivery, registered, or certified mail. If there are a ny deductions made from the security deposit by the landlord, an itemized list of these deductions must also be sent to the tenant by registered or certified mail within 30 days from the termination of the tenancy.

rule.title: Security Deposit Emergency Displacement
rule.requirement: Within 5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation (authorized official notice or 7+ day certification), landlord must return deposit. Within 3 business days of displacement notice, landlord must notify tenant of collection location. Deposit available 30 days in municipality. If not collected, redeposited. If tenant re-enters, may re-pay deposit (1/3 immediately, 1/3 in 30 days, 1/3 in 60 days).
rule.quoted_span:
Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or 
evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit. The law requires the return when either 
an authorized public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or has certified that the 
displacement is expected to continue longer than seven (7) days. Within three (3) business days of 
having received notice of the displacement, the landlord must let the tenant know where the 
security deposit can be collected.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies when authorized public official posts occupancy prohibition notice or certifies 7+ day displacement

rule.title: Fair Housing Discrimination Prohibition
rule.requirement: Illegal for landlord to refuse to rent or discriminate in rental based on: race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, mental/physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rule.quoted_span:
Under State and federal laws, it is illegal for a landlord or rental agency to refuse to rent or 
discriminate in the rental of housing units. The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental decisions; applies to advertising, screening, lease terms
rule.exemptions: Owner-occupied single-family homes; age-restricted housing (familial status only)
rule.sanctions: Up to $10,000 fine for first offense; monetary damages; mandatory rental to complainant

rule.title: Senior Citizen Grace Period for Rent Payment
rule.requirement: Seniors receiving Social Security Old Age Pension, Railroad Retirement Pension, government pension, Social Security Disability, Supplemental Security Income, or Work First New Jersey benefits entitled to 5 business day grace period for rent payment when due on first of month. No delinquency or late charge assessed during grace period. Landlord failure to allow is criminal offense (disorderly person).

Any senior citizen receiving a Social Security Old Page Pension, a Railroad Retirement 
Pension, or any other governmental pension in lieu of a Social Security Old Age Pension, and any 
recipients of Social Security Disability Benefits, Supplemental Security Income, or benefits under 
Work First New Jersey, must be given a period of five (5) business days grace period for payment 
when the rent is due on the first of the month. No delinquency or late charge may be assessed 
during the grace period. Any landlord who fails  to allow this grace period may be criminally 
prosecuted as a disorderly person
